what_happened: Job 20261029-111202-2bpc ("Refuse readings that drop or defer a part the request names") failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 3 of 3 the critic still said the plan needed revising. The critic judged the plan's location sound: the gate in check_reading_acceptance, following check_governance_coverage, with demonstrations that call the real gate. It left two major findings. (1) The parts parser handles only `(N)` markers and Acceptance bullets, so plain `N.` and `N)` numbered requests are never checked, though the accepted reading designed for them. (2) The stem and stop-list rules, as written, do not let a typical criterion cover the standard Steward bullet "A test fails without the change…". The stop list has no stated order, "without" is not in it, and two shared stems are required. That contradicts the plan's own Criterion 6 hand-check and would falsely refuse the most common request shape. It also gave one minor finding (an affirmative pattern inside a quoted complaint still exempts the part) and one nit (Criterion 1 says "real request text", but the plan rebuilds it from the brief). The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria and no failed checks. Nothing was delivered.
cause: The planner specifies matching rules (parts parser, stems, stop list) by reasoning about the intended behavior and hand-checking a few cases. It never executes them against a corpus of real past requests and readings. Specification gaps (unstated order, a missing stop word, forms the reading named but the parser omits) therefore show up only when the critic traces them by hand. The critic has three rounds and keeps no partial plan, so two late majors fail the job even though the location and approach were right. Athena has a replay mechanism for refusal-rule changes, but it runs on the built code. Nothing exercises a plan's rules at planning time, and nothing checks that the plan covers every form the accepted reading lists.
prevention: Before the critic's first round, the planning stage for any job that adds or changes a reading-refusal or matching rule should have to do two things. First, list every input form the accepted reading names and map each to a parser case in the plan. Second, give the rules as a small deterministic spec (ordered stop list, stem threshold) and run it over a stored sample of real past requests and readings, including the standard Steward bullets. The expected refusal count and the false-refusal count must appear in the plan. The critic then checks the measured results instead of hand-tracing, and the plan cannot reach the last round with unmeasured false-refusal risk.
proposed_request: Re-ask of job 20261029-111202-2bpc: Refuse readings that drop or defer a part the request names. In check_reading_acceptance in reading.rs, after the check_governance_coverage step, refuse a stored change/code reading when the request names numbered parts and the reading drops or defers one. Details: (1) Parse parts in all forms the request can use: `(N)`, `N.`, `N)` and Acceptance bullets. (2) Match a part to a criterion by shared stems using an explicit, ordered rule. Strip stop words first, add 'without' to the stop list, and require one shared stem for short parts and two for long parts. Choose the thresholds so the standard Steward bullet 'A test fails without the change…' is covered by an ordinary criterion. (3) Do not let an affirmative pattern inside a quoted or reported sentence exempt a part. (4) Add one line of about 190 bytes to READING_RULES in briefs.rs, keeping the rule section under its 2400-byte cap. Measure the size and do not estimate it. Acceptance: (a) a test that calls the real gate and builds the reading with the scoped_reading helper uses the numbered-parts text of request 20261029-084645-sza7 as stored, or states plainly that it is rebuilt from the brief, and is refused when a part is deferred; (b) tests show `N.` and `N)` requests are checked in the same way as `(N)`; (c) a reading that covers a Steward-bullet request with ordinary criteria is not refused; (d) a criterion states that the higher refusal rate for dropped parts is intended; (e) the rule-section size test passes with the measured byte count. Run the rule over the stored past readings before planning ends and put the false-refusal count in the plan.
